arena.name: voice-arena
arena.title: Voice Arena
arena.question: Can a voice agent's sentences be checked against its sources before the caller hears them, without slowing the call?

headline: On 42 unsupported sentences (4 natural, 38 planted) across 1 held-out scenario, cascade-jev caught 90% while blocking 2.6% of correct sentences, adding 161 ms p95 before the first word at $0.22 per 1,000 calls. Ignoring the limits, cascade-jev-calibrated caught the most (93%), not a significant difference.

pick.name: cascade-jev
pick.reason: Cheapest, then fastest, of the checkers within both limits whose catches don't differ significantly from the leader's.

data.description: 42 simulated calls for two made-up businesses; tuned on one, measured on the held-out other. Includes planted mistakes.

labels.note: Natural sentences are labeled by agreement of two LLM labelers (disagreements dropped); planted mistakes are wrong by construction.

method.rules: Eligible = at most 5% of correct sentences blocked and at most 300 ms p95 added silence; tied = not significantly different from the leader; pick = cheapest, then fastest, tied checker. Latency is p95 silence added before the first word.

outcome.note: Research study for production voice agents, not an enable-ai decision. The check ships as a standalone library (packages/speech-gate).

caveats: Value on real mistakes is unproven. The agent was right ~97% of the time; of its 4 real mistakes the check stopped 1, and most of the catch rate comes from planted mistakes.
Calls are simulated with AI callers, not real customers.
Labels come from LLM labelers, not humans.
